result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): In A, the client, details and line-item groups are separated by spacing alone, with even internal rhythm. However, its totals block sits only slightly farther from the last line item than the items sit from each other, so the separation is weak. B separates the totals clearly with a large gap and uses dividers between sections, but its invoice-details grid has an awkward double rule under the dates and the header-to-Bill To gap is tight. Both put the buttons in a footer separated by a divider, and both screenshots cut off the Save draft button at the bottom. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A divides client, invoice meta, line items and totals with full-width dividers and generous vertical padding, and leaves a clearly larger gap before the totals block. It does have a stray inner rule under the meta grid, and in both screenshots the Save draft button is cut off at the bottom. B relies on section labels with modest spacing, and its totals sit only a line-item-sized gap below the last item, so the grouping hierarchy is weaker and the layout feels tighter.
